properties.name: LESSON: when a property's shape changes, an OLDER binary still running its old schema injects the old default on every write — so a normaliser that merges a legacy value found BESIDE the new shape mints phantom facts; legacy props beside the new shape are stale, never claims
properties.statement:
CONTEXT: AUTHORED_BY moved from single `role` (schema default `author`) to the set `roles`. `validate_edge_properties` inserts a declared default for any missing property on WRITE — measured in code. reflow2's own launch wrapper was, at the time, serving `target/release` at 0.59.0 while the working tree was 0.60.2 — measured off the daemon's `served_by` — so an older binary writing to the same store is not hypothetical here; it was the state of this machine for most of the day.

THE HAZARD (reasoned from those two measurements, not yet reproduced end to end): an old binary touching an AUTHORED_BY edge puts `role: author` back beside `roles: [approver]`. A normaliser that reads `role` as a legacy CLAIM merges it: `roles: [author, approver]`. A phantom author, minted by a schema default, on every edge the old binary touched — the mirror image of the defect being fixed.

THE RULE, now in `normalize_authored_by_props` and pinned by a test: when the NEW shape is present, a legacy property beside it is stale and is DROPPED, not merged. Only an edge with no new shape at all is a legacy edge. Stated generally: on any shape migration, "old prop AND new prop both present" means an old writer has been here since the migration — the new shape is the record.

BOUND: this drops a legacy `role=approver` that an old binary might have MERGED (not replaced) beside a set. No code path in reflow2 merges AUTHORED_BY props — `create_edge` replaces — so that case does not arise today; if a merge-write path is ever added for this edge, this rule needs revisiting.

WHAT WOULD ADDRESS IT IN THE DESIGN: schema defaults injected at write are the root of both this and BL-198 (fact:the-schema-declares-81-defaults-and-nothing-reads-them). A default the WRITER applies is a claim nobody made. A default the READER applies is a fallback nobody stores. Only the second is safe across versions.
